newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran in talks to buy five new oil tankers.
newsitem.headline: Iran in talks to buy five new oil tankers.

text.p: National Iranian Tanker Company (NITC) said on Sunday it was set to buy five new foreign-built crude tankers as part of a plan to modernise its fleet and cut the cost of hiring vessels on the international tanker market.

NITC chairman Mohammad Souri also said talks with shipyards in Japan, South Korea, China and Croatia have centred on a $260 million deal for five Suezmax type tankers that would be used by NITC to sell Iranian crude directly to Mediterranean markets through the Suez Canal.
NITC was studying submitted bids and planned to make a contract award in the next two months for the tankers to be delivered in under two years, he added.
"I hope very shortly we can close (the deal)," Souri told Reuters in an interview at the firm's headquarters.
At present NITC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC), regularly pays hard currency to hire tankers from the international spot market.
It has 10 tankers on time-charter, half of which are usually used for the journey through the canal.
"Better than time-charter is to have our own fleet."

The company took delivery last year of five 300,000 deadweight tonnes Very Large Crude Carriers built by South Korea's Daewoo, partly replacing its ageing and increasingly expensive fleet which was mostly built in the mid-1970s.
A major part of its fleet which survived the 1980-88 war with Iraq and limited investment after Iran's 1979 Islamic revolution has already been scrapped or sold for demolition.

Suezmax cargoes each have a capacity of 155,000 deadweight tonnes -- the maximum size for the Suez Canal -- and would be used to transport Iranian crude to NIOC's customers in Turkey, Italy, Spain, Greece and Romania.
NITC is responsible for exporting 950,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iran's 2.6 million bpd crude exports on a "delivered" or charge, insurance and freight (cif) basis.
Its fleet includes 11 crude tankers and nine product vessels, of which six crude vessels are 20-year-old or more.
The crude tankers have become a potential environmental liability as well as costly because their turbine engines run on expensive bunker fuel and the tankers have high insurance premiums.
The Suezmax cargoes will have double-hulls in line with international shipping laws. They will also have diesel engines.
NITC has planned to gradually buy a further 20 new tankers under Iran's current 1995-2000 plan.
This includes five Aframax cargoes, each with a capacity of 80,000 to 120,000 deadweight tonnes, five product carriers of 45,000 tonnes each, five VLCCs and five more Suezmax.
"We are not going to buy second-hand VLCCs anymore," Souri said.
Iran is the world's third largest oil exporter and relies heavily on the annual $18 billion in hard currency earnings that oil brings.
